subject: Throughput safety corridor forecast for Monarch Labs - capacity inputs needed
messages:
From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Byrne <alicia@monarchlabs.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Throughput safety corridor forecast for Monarch Labs - capacity inputs needed

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. To finalize a committed capacity & pricing proposal we need a short set of inputs from Monarch that feed directly into our GPU sizing model and the safety corridor we recommend. Can you confirm the following by EOD Wednesday?

- Typical tokens per request (median and 95th) and average request size (tokens) for the main LLM endpoint.
- Expected peak TPS or tokens/sec during initial rollout week and steady-state peak after 90 days.
- Target p95 latency SLO (in ms) for end-user calls and whether synchronous blocking is required.
- Percent of traffic that uses long-context flows (>8k tokens) vs short-chat flows.
- Any quiet hours / predictable batching windows (timezone and hours).

I attached a short XLS (safety_corridor_model.xlsx) that shows how those inputs map to GPU slabs, baseline slab counts, and a 15% buffer. We'll run a second pass with Karthik and Neha once you share numbers.

If easier, reply with approximate ranges — we'll use conservative assumptions for the proposal.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
(Attachment: safety_corridor_model.xlsx)

From: Alicia Byrne <alicia@monarchlabs.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@monarchlabs.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2027 11:47:23 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput safety corridor forecast for Monarch Labs - capacity inputs needed

Markus —

Appreciate the checklist. Quick answers below (these are our current best estimates; procurement is looped for SOW visibility):

- Typical tokens per request: median 85 tokens, p95 ~420 tokens.
- Average request size: ~110 tokens (including generation + system tokens).
- Expected peak: initial pilot peak ~6,500 tokens/sec (short bursts), steady-state peak post-90-days ~4,200 tokens/sec.
- Target p95 latency: 600 ms for synchronous user-facing calls. We can have async fallbacks for >2s operations.
- Long-context usage: ~8% of traffic will use >8k contexts (mostly batch summarization jobs), remainder short-chat flows.
- Quiet hours: PST 01:00–05:00 usually low traffic.

We also uploaded the signed SOW v2 to your shared Drive (Monarch_SOW_v2.pdf). Let me know if you want an export of historical request distributions — I can ask ops to push a sample trace.

—Alicia Byrne
VP Product, Monarch Labs
(Attachment referenced: Monarch_SOW_v2.pdf)

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Byrne <alicia@monarchlabs.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2027 08:54:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput safety corridor forecast for Monarch Labs - capacity inputs needed

Alicia —

Thanks for the fast response and the numbers — exactly what we needed. I ran these through our slab-sizing pipeline and pulled a conservative recommendation for the committed capacity package. Summary below (high level):

- Inputs used: p95 tokens/request 420, initial burst peak 6500 tokens/sec, steady-state 4200 tokens/sec, long-context 8%, p95 latency target 600 ms.
- Execution assumptions: using rdx-gpu-slab-64 (quantized open model baseline) delivering ~1,000 tokens/sec per slab at 600 ms p95 for short-chat single-turn calls; long-context jobs degrade slab efficiency by ~35% (KV cache + memory pressure).

Recommended committed package (initial term, monthly average):
- Baseline slabs to meet steady-state 4,200 tps: 5 slabs (5 x 1,000 = 5,000 tokens/sec effective).
- Burst headroom to hit initial pilot peak 6,500 tps: reserve + burst pool of 2 slabs on-demand (expected to be scheduled via Dedicated burst capacity).
- Long-context carveout: we recommend 1 extra slab dedicated for long-context batching to preserve latency on chat flows.
- Safety corridor: add 25% buffer on baseline => final baseline = 6 slabs (5 * 1.25 rounded up).

Net recommended reserve commit: 6 slabs (monthly), with 2-slab burst pool for pilot week. This provides an effective token capacity ~6,000 tokens/sec baseline and ability to absorb 6,500+ bursts with the burst pool and caching.

Estimated latency fit: with the above configuration and our runtime optimizations, we project p95 latency ~520–640 ms depending on prompt mix (long-context requests that hit the carveout will have lower variance).

Estimated monthly unit economics (ballpark):
- Committed slab fee (6 slabs): $78,000/mo
- Burst usage (2 slabs x pilot week estimated 40 hours): ~$3,200 one-off overage in month 1
- Recommended additional line item: monitoring & 7x24 on-call for pilot (optional) ~$6,000/mo

Next steps: 1) Karthik to validate slab-token mapping & confirm kernel/quantization assumptions. 2) Neha to map pricing to the SOW and create a line-item friendly quote. 3) If those checks pass, we’ll prepare the DocuSign SOW and an appendix for the burst policy.

I attached a short capacity brief for Monarch summarizing the numbers and the mapping (monarch_capacity_brief.pdf).

If you want, we can also propose a one-week canary with autoscale rules that restrict burst to predefined windows.

Thanks —
Markus
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: monarch_capacity_brief.pdf)

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2027 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput safety corridor forecast for Monarch Labs - capacity inputs needed

Markus / team — quick confirmation after running the sizing sims:

- Slab mapping looks right under our conservative kernel set: rdx-gpu-slab-64 ~= 1,000 tokens/sec at the 600 ms p95 mark for the short-chat mix. Long-context runs reduce throughput to ~650 tokens/sec per slab.
- The 25% safety corridor is sensible for Monarch given peak burstiness and the 8% long-context mix; it reduces risk of tail amplification during pilot.
- Recommendation: include an operational clause in the SOW limiting unbounded burst otherwise we need to pre-provision an extra slab (cost delta ~$13k/mo). For contracting, call it "burst window guardrails" (time-limited, metered).

I'll sign off on the numbers. Neha — happy to pair on final pricing matrix for the quote.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Inference Ops — Redwood Inference
